text:

# Amazon FSx for Lustre lowers the entry cost of Intelligent-Tiering file systems by 75%

 Posted on: Nov 12, 2026 

Amazon FSx for Lustre is reducing the minimum provisioned throughput capacity and metadata IOPS on Intelligent-Tiering file systems by 75%, allowing you to use Intelligent-Tiering even more cost-effectively for high-performance computing (HPC) and machine learning workloads that start with small datasets and grow over time.

The FSx for Lustre Intelligent-Tiering storage class delivers the lowest-cost and only fully elastic Lustre file storage in the cloud. It is optimized for workloads that mix hot and cold data and do not require consistent SSD-level performance. A file system's throughput capacity determines the read and write speeds supported by its underlying file servers, and its level of metadata IOPS determines how many files and directories you can create, read, and delete per second. Today’s launch reduces the minimum throughput capacity on an Intelligent-Tiering file system from 4,000 to 1,000 MBps and the minimum metadata performance from 6,000 to 1,500 IOPS. 

The lower throughput capacity and metadata IOPS levels are available on new FSx for Lustre Intelligent-Tiering file systems in all AWS Regions where the Intelligent-Tiering storage class is available. To learn more, see Performance characteristics of Intelligent-Tiering storage class in the Amazon FSx for Lustre User Guide.

title: Baseten added Volumes storage to its Sandboxes pricing — PricingSaaS Pulse
text:
Baseten added Volumes storage to its Sandboxes pricing — PricingSaaS Pulse

# Baseten added Volumes storage to its Sandboxes pricing

By Rob Litterst, Co-founder, PricingSaaS

Published Nov 6, 2026 · Last updated Nov 7, 2026

Baseten added Volumes storage to Sandboxes, priced at $0.16 per GB per month.

Baseten’s pricing page · Change detected Nov 6, 2026

## What changed

Baseten added a new "Volumes" line item to the Sandboxes Runtime Pricing rate card, priced at $0.16 per GB per month, per Baseten's pricing page as of Nov 6, 2026. Volumes adds persistent storage to Sandboxes, the usage-based compute product Baseten introduced on Nov 3, 2026, when it replaced its Basic, Pro and Enterprise plan cards with Pay as you go and Production scale tiers.

The addition comes one day after Baseten's last pricing move, when it expanded its Model API rate table with new models, according to Pulse's record. Pulse has tracked 13 Baseten pricing changes since it began following the company on Jul 20, 2026, including 11 in the last 90 days — an average of one every 9 days.

## Why it matters

For a product leader watching usage-based pricing, Baseten's move shows how fast a new rate card gets filled in once it exists. Having replaced its flat Basic, Pro and Enterprise tiers with Sandboxes usage pricing on Nov 3, 2026, Baseten is already adding a standalone metered line item for storage rather than folding it into compute pricing — a sign the company intends Sandboxes pricing to be granular by design, not a stopgap.

$0.16 per GB per month, per Baseten's pricing page as of Nov 6, 2026, is a small number on its own, but it sets a reference point for any team pricing persistent storage alongside compute: workloads that hold state on Sandboxes now show a separate storage line instead of storage bundled into compute minutes. That split makes a usage-based bill easier to read line by line, but harder to predict as a single number.

...

### What would persistent storage cost for a typical Sandboxes workload?

Multiply $0.16 by the gigabytes of persistent storage your Sandboxes workload keeps mounted each month, per Baseten's pricing page as of Nov 6, 2026 — that's the full extra cost; compute is billed separately under the usage pricing Baseten introduced on Nov 3, 2026.

title: MC1330893: SharePoint Pay-As-You-Go Storage Billing
text:
MC1330893: SharePoint Pay-As-You-Go Storage Billing

# MC1330893: SharePoint Online Adds Pay‑as‑You‑Go Consumption‑Based Billing for Extra Storage 

9 November 2026 4 minutes Posted in SharePoint Online Posted by Modern Workspace Pro 

 Recommended Action: Take a look and decide whether this affects your tenant, users or support teams. 

#### Primary Audience 

 Microsoft 365 Admins SharePoint Admins IT Managers Service Owners 

 Why this score? 

 AI Confidence HIGH Enough detail is available to trust this assessment. 

 Assessment Reasoning 

 The announcement moves the general availability date from November 2026 to January 2027. Admins managing SharePoint storage will need to plan for an optional pay‑as‑you‑go billing model linked to Azure subscriptions. The change introduces new cost tracking and governance options but no immediate user impact. Effort centres on planning, permissions and internal cost documentation rather than urgent technical action.

...

### AT A GLANCE 

 SharePoint is adding a pay‑as‑you‑go option for storage overages. This lets you pay for only the extra space you use instead of buying storage upfront. 

### END USERS 

 No major end‑user change expected. 

### IT ADMINS 

 Review your SharePoint storage use, billing setup and documentation before the January 2027 rollout. 

### ROLLOUT TIMELINE 

 Upcoming: January 2027 

### 📢 Official Microsoft Message Center Announcement

(Updated) Pay-as-you-go consumption-based meter for your extra SharePoint storage needs Message ID: MC1330893 (Updated) 

Updated November 9, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[Introduction]

To help organizations manage SharePoint storage more flexibly and avoid over-provisioning, Microsoft is introducing a pay-as-you-go, consumption-based billing model for SharePoint storage overages. This option allows you to pay only for the additional storage you actually use, rather than pre-purchasing extra capacity. The experience integrates with Microsoft 365 Archive and helps align storage costs with real usage.

This change is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 506743.

[When this will happen:]

- Public Preview (Worldwide): We completed rollout in June 2026.
- General Availability (WW): We expect to begin rolling out in early January 2027 (previously early November) and to complete rolling by late January 2027 (previously end of November). 

[How this affects your organization:]

Who is affected:

- Microsoft 365 administrators managing SharePoint Online storage
- Note: This feature isn’t currently available to education tenants. Let us know if you’d like it to be supported in the future.

What will happen:

- Admins can enable pay-as-you-go SharePoint storage billing in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
- Storage used above the included tenant quota will be automatically billed based on consumption.
- There is no impact to users.
- The existing Office 365 Extra File Storage add‑on remains available if you prefer to manually increase your storage quota instead.
- The feature is opt-in and off by default.

[What you can do to prepare:]

- No immediate action is required. However, we recommend the following:
- Review your tenant’s current SharePoint storage usage in the SharePoint admin center > Active sites.
- Evaluate whether a consumption‑based model or manually purchased storage best fits your organization’s cost and governance preferences.
- If you plan to enable pay‑as‑you‑go billing:

- Ensure the appropriate Azure subscription and billing permissions are in place.
- Update internal documentation or cost‑management processes as needed.
- Share this information with finance or procurement teams if they track usage‑based charges.

Learn more: Add more SharePoint storage to your subscription | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

| Compliance area | Impact and explanation |
| --- | --- |
| Admin monitoring and reporting | SharePoint storage usage above the included tenant quota will be reflected in consumption-based billing and usage reports, which may affect how admins monitor and track storage consumption and costs. |
| Admin control | Administrators must explicitly enable |

# Seagate Launches the FireCuda Forge, Powered by New Alkemi Intelligent Platform to Deliver Both SSD-Grade Responsiveness and HDD Capacity 

Alkemi’s dynamic-caching technology prioritizes recent and frequently accessed data on a user-provided SSD while storing high-value, foundational content on a high-capacity hard drive.

SINGAPORE, November 10, 2026 – Seagate Technology Holdings plc (NASDAQ: STX), a mass-capacity data storage leader, today introduced the Seagate® FireCuda™ Forge drive, representing the first Seagate hard drive powered by the Alkemi™ intelligent storage platform. With Alkemi, the FireCuda Forge combines solid-state drive (SSD) responsiveness and hard disk drive (HDD) capacity in a single drive, using adaptive intelligence to give gamers and creators the speed and space they need without added complexity.

...

Engineered to improve with use, the Alkemi dynamic-caching technology learns how data is used in real-time and automatically prioritizes frequently accessed content from a user's SSD, while ensuring the HDD provides capacity for larger libraries. The result brings intelligent data tiering from the data center to the desktop, dynamically caching data based on activity patterns, to deliver fast and easy access without users having to manage where their data lives.

...

FireCuda Forge is the first product to deliver the Alkemi experience, combining a user's NVMe SSD with the Forge's high-capacity HDD to onboard processing in a single box. Seagate engineers designed the FireCuda Forge to provide fast, seamless access to the content people use most, while offering the capacity to keep more of what matters, whether gaming, streaming, creating or managing everyday digital life.

Product highlights

- First product build on the Alkemi platform: Alkemi learns and adapts over time to keep high-demand content fast and accessible on a user’s SSD, while the HDD provides space for growing libraries. Behind the scenes, Alkemi manages data placement, giving users the simplicity of a single storage drive.
- Performance for demanding workflows: Up to 2,500MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write performance.
- Choice and expandability: The FireCuda Forge contains an upgradeable HDD, and users select and provide their own NVMe SSD that is required for operational compatibility.
- High-bandwidth connectivity: USB4 supports gaming and creator workflows on compatible systems.
- Platform support: Designed to support Windows 11 and macOS 26 and above.

Availability: The FireCuda Forge is available now through the Seagate on-line store and authorized partners in 8TB and 20TB configurations, starting at $699 (8TB) and $899 (20TB). Product availability may vary by market.

title: No Gate, No Wait: Introducing CNQ Spark
text:
No Gate, No Wait: Introducing CNQ Spark

# No Gate, No Wait: Introducing CNQ Spark

November 11, 2026

James Walkenhorst

There is an old ritual in enterprise storage, and anyone who has ever evaluated a product knows every step of it. 

You request a demo. 

You wait for a call. 

You get a license. 

And then, days or weeks after the moment that first sparked your curiosity, you finally get to touch the thing you wanted to try. 

For some buyers, that ritual is perfectly reasonable. For the engineer or builder or architect who is used to standing up whatever they need without asking anyone's permission, it is a gate in front of a door they could have opened themselves. By the time the call gets scheduled, the afternoon they had free for this is long gone.

Today we are announcing CNQ Spark, a real, fully working Qumulo deployment that lands in your own subscription in less than 10 minutes. Scan a code or follow a link while logged into your own Azure account, and build a fast, nimble data platform that works natively with any SMB, NFS, or object workload from a single virtual machine. No license request. No call with sales. No waiting. Spark sweeps all the old gates aside.

...

Spark isn't that. It runs the same Qumulo Core file engine, and exposes the same REST API, that a paying customer's cluster does. Nothing about it is a simulation. Here is what that means in practice:

- One namespace, three protocols. NFS, SMB and S3, all against the same data at the same time. Drop a file in through one protocol and pick it up through another.
- Your own Active Directory. Join your own domain and test against your actual identity infrastructure, not a synthetic one built for the occasion.
- Snapshots, the same as on any Qumulo cluster.
- Live analytics. Throughput, IOPS, latency and capacity, charted in Grafana as the workload runs.
- Three ways to manage it. A web UI, a terminal UI, and the full REST API. Use whichever you like, or all three. Whatever you do in one is just a call to the same API underneath (with one note: S3/object is included but disabled by default. Use the API to enable and configure object support)

...

## What it costs

There is no Qumulo license and no subscription fee, and there never will be. You pay Azure for the virtual machine and storage that Spark uses, exactly as you would for any other workload, and nothing more. Every Spark VM comes with 1 TB of capacity.

## What Spark is not

Spark is for scratch data, development and evaluation. We want to be plain about that.

It runs on a single node, and its resilience comes from the Azure managed disk beneath it, not from Qumulo's multi-node erasure coding. It has no built-in data protection. If the virtual machine fails or restarts, you should expect to lose what was on it. So don’t put anything in Spark that you can't afford to lose. When a workload starts to matter, that is exactly what a protected, multi-node Azure Native Qumulo deployment is for.

# Hippius Mobile App Is Live: Download for Cheaper Cloud Storage

Hippius Mobile is live on the App Store and Google Play. Back up any file automatically, encrypted on your device, at about 30% less than Dropbox or Google.

Hippius Team

November 9, 2026

We're excited to announce that the Hippius Mobile app is live today on the App Store and Google Play, bringing the full Hippius Drive to iOS and Android for the first time. It's the same Hippius account behind the desktop app and web console, now in your pocket. Any file syncs and backs up automatically, encrypted on your device before it ever leaves. Plans are month-to-month with no contract, and less than what Dropbox or Google charge for the same amount of storage. If you've been weighing up cloud storage alternatives, or thinking about moving from Dropbox or Google Drive, Hippius now works the same way on every device you use.

...

The mobile app brings the core of Hippius Drive to a phone for the first time: full cloud storage for any file, not just photos. Camera Uploads backs up your photos in the background as you take them, sorting everything into images, videos, docs, and more, so you always know what's using space. Files sync the same way they do on desktop: encrypted on your device before upload, so Hippius never sees an unencrypted copy.

Signing in uses the same options as the web console: Google, GitHub, Apple, or an access key.

...

## Plans and Pricing: Less Than Dropbox or Google Drive

New Hippius accounts get 10 GB free, so there's room to start backing up right away. From there, paid plans are month-to-month, with no long-term contract. Plans start as low as $4 per month. See full pricing here.

At the 2 TB mark (the tier most people land on), Hippius is $7 per month. That's 30% less than Dropbox and Google's 2 TB plan, which are both listed at $9.99/month.

Plans and credits themselves are managed from the web console at console.hippius.com. Sign in there to pick a plan or add credits, and it applies everywhere, mobile and desktop included, since it's all the same account.

...

### How much does Hippius cost compared to Dropbox or Google Drive?

Less, at the same storage size. A 2 TB Hippius plan is $7/month with no contract, versus around $9.99/month for Dropbox's or Google's 2 TB plans. Each plan scales in the same pattern (whereby Hippius is more affordable), plus you get 10 GB for free to start with Hippius.

## What does cloud storage cost in 2026?

Personal cloud storage costs between about $1.80 and $16 per TB a month on plans up to 10 TB in November 2026, depending on the service and the plan size. - Per-user pricing. Dropbox plans above 2 TB are team plans priced per user, and Advanced needs at least three people, from $90 a month.
- Transfer quotas. MEGA limits how much you can download each month, and pCloud caps shared-link downloads at twice your storage.
- Paid add-ons. pCloud's folder encryption costs an extra $4.99 a month.
- Currency and tax. MEGA, Filen, Internxt and some Proton plans charge in euros, and every price here is before tax.
